message.content: Logistic regression is a statistical technique used for binary classification problems. It models the probability that a given input belongs to one of two classes (e.g., success/failure, yes/no) by applying the logistic (sigmoid) function to a linear combination of the input features. The resulting output is a value between 0 and 1, which can be interpreted as a probability or converted into a class label using a threshold (commonly 0.5). Logistic regression estimates parameters that maximize the likelihood of observing the training data, and it provides interpretable coefficients that reflect the influence of each feature on the log‑odds of the outcome.
